description: Council reviewed 2026/2027 budget options to reduce future tax increases.
Administration will report on city spending on other governments' responsibilities.

chips.text: Received as information
Councillor Jeffries questioned the Chamber's data on city spending outpacing inflation.
Saskatoon businesses and taxpayers are affected by potential property tax increases.
Business groups urged Council to control spending, limit tax increases, and explore AI/outsourcing.
Options include funding for affordable housing incentives and homelessness response programs.
Mayor Block promised a business forum and survey for business license holders.

speakers.name: Jason Aebig
speakers.summary: Jason Aebig, Greater Saskatoon Chamber of Commerce, addressed the Committee urging Council to control spending like businesses do, rather than relying on tax increases.
said: Businesses control spending, expect city to do same
City spending outpaced growth, frustrating commercial taxpayers
Demand savings, use AI/outsourcing to reduce tax burden

speakers.name: Keith Moen
speakers.summary: Keith Moen, NSBA, addressed the Committee urging Council to limit tax increases, pursue fiscal restraint, consider workforce reductions and AI adoption, and act on cost-saving recommendations to ensure sustainable city finances.
said: Pace of tax increases is not sustainable
Council must direct administration to find efficiencies
Limit new hires, reduce workforce, embrace AI for savings
